la:verb:suo.html:
sŭo, sŭi, sūtum, 3, v. a.
Sanscr. siv-, sivjāmi, sew; Gr. κασσύω, to stitch, cobble
,
to sew or stitch, to sew, join, or tack together (rare but class.).
Lit.: quod (foramen) nisi permagnā vi sui non potest,: tegumenta corporum vel texta vel suta,: unius os sutum,: pellibus et sutis arcent male frigora bracis,: hi plerasque naves loris suebant, Varr. ap. : navis suta lino et sparteis serilibus, Pac. ap. Fest. s. v. serilla, p. 340 fin. Müll. (Trag. Rel. v. 251 Rib.): corticibus suta cavatis alvearia,: pilea suta de caesis lacernis,. — *
Trop.: metue lenonem, ne quid suo suat capiti,devise,; cf. consuo, II. — Hence, P. a. as subst.: sūta, ōrum, n., that which is made of plates fastened together, mail, a coat of mail: huic gladio perque aerea suta Per tunicam squalentem auro latus haurit apertum,: magnorum aerea suta Thoracum,: latus omne sub armis Ferrea suta terunt,.
